title: 3. Obtaining Approvals
text:
Obtaining necessary approvals is essential for beginning the data collection process. Since approval requirements vary by country, this step provides a list of common approvals. The examples provided are from previous implementations, but GEPD’s implementation team should always meet country-specific regulatory needs.
Certain approvals are necessary to ensure ethical standards are met, particularly when the data collection involves sensitive activities such as interviewing and assessing children, as well as conducting classroom observations. These approvals safeguard the rights and well-being of participants, especially minors.
Sample of Types of Approvals that might be needed:

Ethical Approval - (if applicable).
Approvals requested from the National Statistics Agency - (if applicable).

The Approvals topic can be approached during the Initial Meeting, where the specific approvals required in the country through for the data collection can be clarified in the discussions with government officials.
To comprehensively address these requirements, the local team must collaborate closely with the Survey Firm. In most implementations, it is the Survey Firm that bears the primary responsibility for securing all necessary approvals, ensuring that the data collection process adheres to both local and international ethical guidelines.



 Back to top

title: 2. Selecting Sample
text:
The Global Education Policy Dashboard (GEPD) uses a two-stage random sampling method for collecting representative and quality data. Initially, schools are selected through a stratified sampling based on urban/rural classification and, if needed, geographical regions. This step guarantees a diverse and accurate representation of the nation’s schools. The second stage involves randomly selecting teachers and students from these schools for interviews and assessments.

School SamplingPublic Officials Sampling



Request & Receive the Country’s List of Schools
The Sampling Tool can only be used when the Country share the Country’s List of Schools file, that can also be downloaded here School List - this is the same list previously discussed with country at the substep 1.4 of Confirming Country’s Participation. Such list contains the following columns, to be populated:

Name of School: Official name of the educational institution.
School Code: Unique identifier for the school.
Region: Geographical region where the school is located.
District: Administrative district of the school’s location.
City: City or town where the school is situated.
Geographic Location: School’s specific geographical coordinates.
Urban or Rural Indicator: Classification as urban or rural.
Type of School: Category or kind of school (e.g., primary).
Type of Property: Ownership status of the school building.
Does the school have a second shift? Yes/No: Indicator of dual-shift system.
1st Grade Total Number of Students: Total students in 1st grade.
2nd Grade Total Number of Students: Total students in 2nd grade.
3rd Grade Total Number of Students: Total students for 3rd grade.
th Grade Total Number of Students: Total students for 4th grade.
5th Grade Total Number of Students: Total students in 5th grade.
Total of Teachers: Total teachers in the school.



Sampling Rules:
The rules for running the random stratification when sampling are:

Sample size: GEPD common sample size is of 200 to 300 schools;
Stratification: GEPD uses the rural/urban classification as a Strata when sampling. The region column is optional, but including it can influence the overall sample size
Minimum of students: to qualify as a valid sample school, each school must have a minimum of three (3) students in both 1st and 4th grades.



Steps for Using the Sampling Tool:

Upload your excel or csv file containing the list of schools
Choose the sample size of schools (from 200 to 300 sample size)
Choose one or two columns that you want to use for stratification
Run the sampling!
Visualize the schools selected
Download your file containing the schools sampled
Document the steps of your sampling process
Reach out to the Central Team as needed



This Sampling Tool was created to assist you during the Sampling Process of GEPD’s Implementation. You can also access the source code used to generate the stratified sample by downloading it: Download Sampling R Code



In the GEPD implementation, the sampling of public officials involves selecting 200 public education officials, focusing on personnel from both central and regional/district offices of the Ministry of Education. The sampling utilizes a cluster strategy. However, most commonly, instead of receiving a direct list of public officials, GEPD is typically provided with a list of regional and district public office locations.
Based on this, 10 regional offices are randomly selected from the regions corresponding to the school survey. In each region, one district office is chosen. Within these offices, the sampling includes 7 officials: the head of the office, the HR director, and five randomly chosen officials from finance and planning.
The federal level sampling is conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, focusing on key offices, where the director and a random selection of officials are interviewed. This stratified approach ensures comprehensive coverage from school to district, regional, and central offices.

Step-by-step

Receive Office Locations List
Select Regional Offices: randomly choose 10 regional offices from the provided list, ensuring they align with the regions where schools were surveyed.
Choose District Offices: In each selected region, randomly pick one district office
Sample Officials in Offices:

In each regional/district office, randomly select 7 officials, including the office head, HR director, and five officials from finance and planning.
At the federal level, work with the Ministry of Education to identify relevant offices. Interview the office director and a random number of staff members.

Document the sampling process

title: 9. Validating the Results
text: The validation of results is a critical step in ensuring that the data collected is understood and owned by the country. This is achieved by holding a stakeholder validation session with the country’s public officials before dissemination. The goal of the session is to ensure that the government can effectively use the data to inform policy decisions.

title: 9. Validating the Results
text:
9.1 - Prepare the Presentation

The World Bank team prepares a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the key survey results. The content is agreed upon by both the GEPD and country teams.
This presentation is used during the stakeholder validation session to facilitate discussions on the key findings.

title: 9. Validating the Results
text:
9.2 - Coordinate the Validation Session

The World Bank country team sets the date for the validation session - that can happen in-person or remote - and invites relevant government officials. Key development partners and the survey firm may also be invited.
The session usually lasts 1.5-2 hours, starting with the World Bank team presenting the results, followed by a discussion with the participants.

title: 9. Validating the Results
text:
9.3 - Address Questions and Make Revisions

The World Bank team answers any questions or clarifies details that arise during the session. Any additional resources (such as notes on sampling) can be shared as needed.
If the government requests changes, these are discussed and incorporated where appropriate.

title: 9. Validating the Results
text:
9.4 - Finalizing the Data

If there are no objections from the government after the session, the data is considered ready for publication.

title: 6. Training Enumerators and Piloting
text:
Training and piloting are critical to the successful implementation of GEPD. Training sessions vary depending on the survey: School Survey training spans five days due to the need for careful handling of assessments involving children and because it covers a higher amount of modules, while the Public Officials Survey training can last two to five complete days.
It should be taken into consideration that the training sessions can either be implemented sequentially or in parallel, adapting to resource availability and logistical constraints. Paralell implementation would mean having two sets of enumreators being trained at the same time, each in a different Instrument

title: 6. Training Enumerators and Piloting
text:
6.1. Differentiated Training Sessions

School Survey Training
Five days of comprehensive training, focusing on the 1:1 assessment methodology with first graders. The School Survey collects data primarily on Practices (the quality of service delivery in schools), but also on some de facto Policy and school-level Politics indicators. It consists of streamlined versions of existing instruments—including Service Delivery Indicator (SDI) Surveys, Teach, Global Early Child Development Database (GECDD), In-Service Teacher Training Instrument Survey (ITTSI), and the Development World Management Survey (DWMS)—together with new questions to fill gaps in those instruments.
The School Survey includes 8 short modules: Roster, School Information, Principal Questionnaire, Teacher Questionnaire, Classroom Observation, Teacher Assessment, Direct Assessment, and Student Assessment. For a team of two enumerators, it takes on average about 4 hours to collect all information in a given school.


Public Officials Survey Training
Two to five days focused on understanding administrative data and conducting professional interviews. The Public Officials Survey collects data on the quality of service delivery in public sector organizations and it is comprised of 4 key modules: National Learning Goals (NLG), Accountability and Mandates (ACM), Quality of Bureaucracy (QB), Impartial Decision-making (IDM)

title: 6. Training Enumerators and Piloting
text:
6.2. Utilizing Training Materials

Ensure all training materials, including the manual and the step-by-step guide, are readily available and tailored to the specifics of each survey type.


Resources Available for 6.2:

Download Training Materials - School Survey:

Instruments | Training Manual | Step-by-Step Guide | Training Agenda & Presentations

Download Training Materials - Public Officials:

Instruments | Training Manual | Step-by-Step Guide | Training Agenda & Presentations

title: 6. Training Enumerators and Piloting
text:
6.3. Pilot Testing

Conduct pilot tests in schools not part of the main sample to allow enumerators to practice and refine survey tools. This step is crucial to ensure that the survey tools are well understood and that enumerators are comfortable with the data collection process.
Here, exists the possibility of integrating the feedback collected from enumerators during the training to adjust tools and questions to better fit the local context. This means that, after piloting, there is still some room to adjusting some of the wording or the way questions are asked.

title: 1. Confirming Country’s Participation
text:
Step 1’s primary goal is to secure a country’s participation in the Global Education Policy Dashboard (GEPD). This process begins with identifying a potential need for the GEPD in a country and then arranging and conducting an initial meeting to present the Dashboard.
A follow-up email is sent post-meeting to confirm participation and outline the next steps and most immediate actions required. Finally, once participation is confirmed, the TTL coordinates communication accordingly, guaranteeing the necessary information exchange.

title: 1. Confirming Country’s Participation
section: 1.1 - Opportunity Window: Identifying a need for the Dashboard
text:
1.1 - Opportunity Window: Identifying a need for the Dashboard
At this moment, the task is to pinpoint a specific need within a country that the GEPD can effectively address. This process might involve analyzing situations where the Dashboard can serve as a potent solution. These needs can be identified proactively by investigating the country’s education policy landscape or in response to a direct request from the country. The goal is to establish the GEPD as a fitting tool that aligns with the country’s educational objectives and challenges.

title: 1. Confirming Country’s Participation
text:
1.2 - Requesting an Initial Meeting
In this phase, the focus shifts to the TTL arranging an initial meeting with key stakeholders in the potential counterpart country. This meeting is planned to last 60-90 minutes, and is intended to delve deeper into the Dashboard’s capabilities and relevance to the country’s needs. Preparation for this meeting involves sending a well-crafted introductory email to the country’s representatives, accompanied by essential GEPD’s resources and the link for GEPD’s Website. These documents should provide more details on the Dashboard, illustrating its capacity to meet the country’s specific data requirements.

Resources Available for 1.2:

title: 1. Confirming Country’s Participation
text:
1.3 - Conducting the Meeting
Once the initial meeting is set, the TTL prepares to lead the discussion. The suggested agenda for the meeting is for it to start with a 20-minute presentation on the GEPD, utilizing the provided sample presentation, which needs to be tailored for the country in question. The presentation aims to give a comprehensive overview of the Dashboard’s functionality and benefits. Following the presentation, the TTL dedicates the remaining time to address various key aspects, such as:

Responding to questions about the project’s scope, objectives, and potential impact.
Discussing the specifics of the implementation process.
Detailing the requirements from the country:

Appointing a focal point;
Providing necessary information for sampling;
Understanding the required approvals documents.

Aiming to confirm the country’s participation in the GEPD

title: 1. Confirming Country’s Participation
section: 1.4 - Next Steps Email (following-up after Initial Meeting)
text:
1.4 - Next Steps Email (following-up after Initial Meeting)
After the initial meeting, the following action is to send a comprehensive follow-up email to the country’s representatives. This email should be structured to provide clarity and direction, ensuring the country’s representatives are fully informed of the requirements and upcoming phases in the GEPD implementation process. Its essential purposes are:

Reiteration and Documentation: It includes the presentation delivered during the meeting as an attachment, serving as a reference point and reinforcing the discussed topics.
Confirmation of Participation: If the country’s participation was confirmed during the meeting, the email will formally acknowledge this and express appreciation for the commitment.
Outlining Next Steps: Importantly, the email will detail the subsequent steps required to move the GEPD project forward. This includes:

Creating a project timeline, providing a clear schedule of activities and milestones.
Requesting sample data for the schools and public officials survey, guided by the attached Excel table format.
Establishing contact with the focal point to facilitate data collection and follow-up communications.
Provide the counterpart with all the actions needed from their side



Resources Available for 1.4:

title: 1. Confirming Country’s Participation
text:
1.5 - Establishing Channels of Communication
Once the country’s participation is confirmed and the first communications starts to happen, the TTL’s role shifts towards maintaining momentum and ensuring effective communication. The primary focus at this stage involves two critical aspects:

Refining the Project Timeline: The TTL must work closely with the country’s team to develop a comprehensive timeline for the GEPD implementation. This timeline should outline all key phases, milestones, and deadlines, providing a clear roadmap for the project.
Facilitating Information and Data Exchange: Ongoing interaction between the TTL and the country’s team is essential. The TTL will coordinate the exchange of necessary information and data, ensuring that both sides have what they need for successful implementation. This exchange is crucial for tailoring the GEPD to the country’s specific needs.

The TTL should approach this phase with a focus on clear, consistent communication and collaboration. Keeping the lines of communication open will ensure that any challenges or questions are promptly addressed, and the project stays on track.

text:
The final step is to share the finalized data with the GEPD central team. While the central team handles the publication process on the official website, the country team is responsible for preparing and submitting the data in the required format.

text: Survey firms are selected through competitive bidding - a procurement process, aligned with the Bank standards that spans about eight weeks. The process begins with drafting an Expression of Interest (EOI) letter and Terms of Reference (TOR). Once these documents are ready, the local team initiates the competitive procurement process at the Bank’s RFX Platform.

text:
4.1. Ensure RFX’s Accreditation

Confirm that you or someone in the team - with powers to have it - have the necessary RFX accreditation to use the World Bank’s procurement platform. This is essential for initiating and managing the procurement process.
RFX’s Platform has a lot of resources available teaching how to be properly used. In an extra section that can be found at the bottom of this page we share some of them.

4.5. Score Matching received Proposals & Identifying Winning Firm

After the EOI deadline, review all submissions and shortlist firms based on their initial proposals. Proposals will then be scored on how well they meet the technical requirements outlined in the ToR. title: 5. Preparing Field Work
text:
Step 5 focuses on preparing the field work. This step begins with a detailed onboarding email for the selected survey firm, ensuring they are well-informed and equipped with all necessary resources. The email should also contain an invitation for a kick-off meeting to align everyone’s understanding of the project scope, timeline, and specific roles.

title: 5. Preparing Field Work
section: 5.3. Introduce the Firm to Survey Solutions
text:
5.3. Introduce the Firm to Survey Solutions
As part of the fieldwork preparation, it’s crucial to integrate the Survey Solutions tool for managing and deploying surveys effectively. This involves granting the survey firm access and providing necessary training on using the platform.
Steps to Integrate Survey Solutions:

Granting Access: the survey firm will receive access to the Survey Solutions platform through a headquarters account. This allows them to work with the instrument, manage data collection, but does not grant them the ability to modify the survey design directly.
Technical Session: for the TTL this is likely the most relevant part within this sub-step. A technical session is necessary to train the survey firm on using Survey Solutions. This session covers essential topics like user creation, assignment setup, and understanding the approval process. Typically, the firm learns to create users and set up assignments in bulk, manage interviews, and monitor data collection.
Piloting Phase: before full deployment, the firm will use Survey Solutions to run a pilot test. This phase is critical for identifying any issues with the survey instrument or data collection process. During piloting, the firm can provide feedback on question clarity and flow, which the team can address before the full rollout. Understanding how to version control works within the platform is key here.
Translations and Version Control: survey Solutions allows for easy accommodation of multiple languages through a downloadable template for translation - which after translation needs to be uploaded to the platform. Each country implementation can use its customized version, with the ability to toggle between languages on the platform.

A very useful resource for this step is the Technical Session Manual, generously produced by a GEPD’s member. This guide is an essential resource for the survey firm, helping them familiarize themselves with the tool’s functionalities and ensuring a smoother onboarding process. It includes details on:

Accessing the Survey Solutions platform
Creating users and assignments
Installing Survey Solutions Apps
Monitoring data collection
Downloading data


Resources Available for 5.3:

section: 5.4. Supervising the Preparations of the Firm
text:
5.4. Supervising the Preparations of the Firm
The final step of Preparing the Field Work concerns the TTL responsibility of supervising the survey firm’s preparations, ensuring they meet GEPD standards and adhere to project timelines. This role might involve:

Ensuring the Survey Firm have access to all necessary materials
Overseeing the Survey Firm’s training process and pre-tests of the tools
Overseeing the instrument adaptation, translations and elaboration of the field protocols
Addressing the Survey Firm questions about the survey methodologies

The TTL must also confirm that logistical plans for field work are finalized. Regular check-ins are key for assessing the firm’s progress and addressing potential issues promptly.

title: The Implementation Package
text:
After thirteen implementations of the Global Education Policy Dashboard, all of which happened with a close partnership with regional teams, the central team is excited to present this Implementation Package. It is a comprehensive toolkit that aids in deploying the GEPD’s innovative instruments – the School Survey, Policy Survey, and Survey of Public Officials – with efficiency and effectiveness. It aims to equip local teams with step-by-step guides, practical tools, and all necessary resources for seamless data collection and analysis.
The goal of the Package is to empower local teams with the means to illuminate the often-unseen drivers of learning outcomes, turning insights into actionable strategies for educational advancement. It gives structured guidance throughout the entire process of school visits, classroom observations, and all the moments of engaging with educational stakeholders, ensuring that the GEPD can be implemented with precision and minimal complexity.



Step-by-step GEPD Implementation

title: Global Education Policy Dashboard
text:
Addressing the Learning Crisis
Policymakers in low - and middle - income countries who are working to improve student learning often find themselves flying blind. They see the budget that goes into education and (sometimes) the learning that students come out with, but they lack information on many of the crucial factors in between—the practices, policies, and politics—that drive those learning outcomes. The Global Education Policy Dashboard (GEPD) shines a light on those hidden drivers. To tackle the learning crisis, achieving and sustaining learning gains at scale, countries need to know where they stand on all three of these dimensions—practices (or service delivery), policies, and politics.

title: Global Education Policy Dashboard
text:
The Dashboard
The Global Education Policy Dashboard (GEPD), developed by the World Bank’s Education Global Practice, can help countries reduce Learning Poverty. This tool offers a strong basis for identifying priorities for investment and policy reforms that are suited to each country context. It does so by (1) highlighting gaps between what the evidence suggests is effective in promoting learning and what is happening in practice in each system; and (2) allowing governments to track progress as they take action to close those gaps. The GEPD has been implemented in seven education systems and preparation is ongoing in eight more with expected completion by the end of 2024.
GEPD collects new data in each country using three new instruments: a School Survey, a Policy Survey, and a Survey of Public Officials. Data collection involves school visits, classroom observations, legislative reviews, teacher and student assessments, and interviews with teachers, principals, and public officials. A major objective of the GEPD project was to develop focused, cost-effective instruments and data-collection procedures, so that the dashboard can be inexpensive enough to be applied (and re-applied) in many countries.

title: 7. Collecting the Data
text: Implementing a successful data collection involves working close to the Survey Firm to monitor and assess their implementation plan. At this stage, the survey firm develops an implementation plan considering educational and geographical specifics of the country, including seasonal and logistical challenges. The TTL’s job is to monitor the execution of this plan to ensure all targeted schools are surveyed, addressing any deviations or obstacles encountered.

title: 7. Collecting the Data
text:
7.1. Review the Implementation Plan
The implementation plan is crafted and provided by the Survey Firm, It must be comprehensive, addressing all potential challenges such as the local school calendar, typical weather conditions that might affect travel, and potential school closures. This plan should detail a weekly schedule that outlines how many schools are to be visited each week, ensuring that logistical and regional specifics are considered. The Task Team Leader (TTL) will utilize this plan as a guide to collaborate with the Survey Firm throughout the data collection phase, ensuring that all aspects of the project align with the ground realities.

title: 7. Collecting the Data
text:
7.2. Monitor Weekly Progress
Track the progress against the plan. If fewer schools are covered than planned, investigate the causes and coordinate with local educational authorities if necessary. The TTL should also ensure that the survey firm is adhering to the agreed-upon quality standards. A point of attention here is how many schools are being visited per day, and how much need there was of replacing schools - something that could affect the quality of the sampling, if replacemente is too high.

title: 7. Collecting the Data
7. Collecting the Data
section: 7.4. Facilitate Problem Solving and Adjust the Plan
text:
7.4. Facilitate Problem Solving and Adjust the Plan
Actively engage in solving any problems that arise during data collection, such as access issues to schools or unexpected school closures. The TTL should be prepared to adjust the implementation plan as necessary to ensure that all schools are surveyed within the planned timeline.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
text:
This guide provides detailed instructions on how to go from the raw data extracted from Survey Solutions, a software for data collection and survey management, to the production of a set of data and files essential for assessing national educational outcomes, specifically:
The GEPD collects country-level data through administering a survey with a set of modules:
Main language: Stata 17 and higher (note that older versions of Stata are not compatible)
Assisting language & tools: R, RStudio and GitHub Desktop
Note: Ensure that both software installations are installed and updated before running the code.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
section: 8.1 - Cloning the GitHub folder to your local device
text:
8.1 - Cloning the GitHub folder to your local device
Inside each country’s folder/repository, the data workflow is organized across four sub-folders:

01_GEPD_raw_data; contains the raw data files downloaded from the GEPD Survey Solutions Server. This folder contains three subfolders: a School folder for school data, a Public_Officials folder for data from the Survey of Public Officials, and a Policy_Survey folder for data from the expert Policy Survey. The raw data is downloaded from Survey Solution and is saved on OneDrive inside the respective country folder and synced with GitHub.
02_programs; contains the scripts that will be used to clean and process the raw data. There are separate sub-folders for each of the three data sources: School, Public_Officials, and Policy_Survey.

03_GEPD_processed_data; contains the cleaned and anonymized data files. There are separate sub-folders for each of the three data sources: School, Public_Officials, and Policy_Survey.

04_GEPD_Indicators; contains the set of final GEPD indicators.

Note: Before working with the data, the user must first set-up the GitHub’s country folder/repository on the local machine either as “local repository” or “cloned repository”.

8.1.1 - Adding local repository (recommended)
This is the recommended process if using a WB machine/VDI and having access rights to OneDrive where the data is stored.
On GitHub Desktop, click <<File>>, <<Add local repository>>, choose the country folder on OneDrive, then <<Add repository>>.


8.1.2 - Clone the GitHub repository
Alternatively, if the above-mentioned case is not applicable, a user could clone the GitHub country folder to their local device.

On the internet browser, go to the country’s repo on GitHub.
At the top right of the GitHub page, right click on the <<Code>> tab, then select the option to open the folder with GitHub Desktop.
Set the directory path to where you would like the clone to be placed, then click <<Clone>>.

These steps will create an exact copy of this GitHub folder on your local computer with all the necessary folder structure, Stata code files and the template files needed to reproduce the GEPD indicators.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
section: 8.2 - Downloading the raw data from Survey Solutions to the cloned folder
text:
8.2 - Downloading the raw data from Survey Solutions to the cloned folder
After the GitHub folder is cloned, the sub-folder 01_GEPD_raw_data would be sub-divided into folders corresponding to the survey level: School, Public_Officials, Policy_Survey, and Sampling. The user must download and place the raw data files, from Survey Solutions, into the corresponding sub-folder. Please note: these raw data files are loaded once into Stata, and any processing to it will be saved as a copy into a different Cleaned folder as we are going to explain later —the user must avoid altering or overwriting the raw files.
The user must download all the data files related to:

school, teachers, Grade 1, and Grade 4 students into the School sub-folder.

public officials into the Public_Officials sub-folder.

Policy survey into Policy_Survey sub-folder.

Sampling and weights into Sampling sub-folder.

The process of downloading the data is as straightforward as: (a) signing in to the administrator account on the GEPD server on Survey Solutions with the relevant credentials, (b) selecting to the relevant country workspace (in the top left corner), (c) navigating to Data Export at the top panel and selected the survey template to export as well as the status Approved by HQ, and, (d) downloading all relevant questionnaire data (school survey and survey of public officials) related to this country. Typically, the data is exported in Stata 14 format and includes meta information.
To guide the user on which modules are being administered in each country, one can create a pdf download of the questionnaire in Survey Solutions Designer, open the questionnaire and select ‘Download PDF’ from the buttons in the top right corner of the interface. This will produce an HTML document containing questions divided by module, together with the variable names, answer options and skip patterns/constraints.
A list is provided in the annex of what raw data files a user is expected to see downloaded into the raw data folder. A user may also note that the provided list is only a guidance, and it is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all raw data files that must exist across all countries.
Note: If you do not have a Survey Solutions account, please get in touch with the GEPD team at educationdashboard@worldbank.org

title: 8. Computing Indicators
text:
8.3 - Running the initialization do-files
Before running any of the processing code files, a user must run the initialization do-files located in the main folder titled GEPD_CountryX. These do-files will set the parameters and file paths for the code to run.

GEPD_parameters.do allows the user to set the parameters specific to the country by specifying country name, year, strata, weight variables and file names, etc. Please adjust if needed for each country as some parameters may differ.
profile_GEPD.do should be opened in the same Stata console as parameters.do and allows for setting up file paths and data directories. Please note that this do-file would prompt the user to select on-screen the run_GEPD.do inside the countries folder. Ensure to select the correct run_GEPD.do which is inside the country folder where the data is stored.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
section: 8.4 - Running the cleaning and processing do-files
text:
8.4 - Running the cleaning and processing do-files
After executing the previous step, on the same opened STATA console, run the processing do-files. The folder 02_programs\School includes three do-files needed to produce the necessary cleaned and merged datasets, which a user can either run at once by running the master script 01_school_run, or individually. Either case, please ensure that the following do-files are loaded in the same Stata session/console that ran the parameters and profile do-files:

01_school_run is the master do-file which runs all the three following scripts.
02_school_data_merge runs a program to merge variables from the sampling frame (weights, strata and other observable characteristics such as the location of the school) to each of the school-level datasets (g1 students, g4 students, teachers and school modules). In addition, it merges teachers’ modules and includes all the possible corrections for data entry mistakes in the school-level datasets. The input data is the downloaded raw data which is prespecified in the script. The outcome is four data files for each of those groups and are saved automatically in 03_GEPD_processed \School\Confidential\Merged.
Note on merging teachers’ modules:
Teachers are being surveyed in different modules (hence different datasets) and all the teachers’ data can be downloaded as separate data files from Survey Solutions. However, for the processing do-files to work as intended, teachers’ modules must be combined into a single data file. A heritage procedure attempts to do that using a fuzzy matching technique, which was developed to overcome the issue of the same teacher with different IDs across modules. Note that this step is unnecessary for future implementations of the GEPD of the GEPD (as well as for the Punjab and Sindh provinces of Pakistan, and Edo State in Nigeria), since the teachers in these surveys have consistent IDs across modules. More information on fuzzy matching can be found in the annex.
To combine teachers’ modules, a user would need to execute a “joinby” command, or similar commands, which matches all modules based on two key variables “interview_key” and “teachers_id”.The Stata scrip that merges teachers’ modules is titled <<02_school_data_merge.do>> and highlighted above in point 2. Once the teachers’ modules are merged, the resulting teachers file is saved in the School sub-folder under 01_GEPD_raw_data with the title “Country_teacher_level_test.dta”
03_school_data_cleaner cleans the data produced from the previous step and aggregates correlated variables to produce the GEPD indicators. The outcome is the four data files, as above, but cleaned, for each of those groups and are stored automatically in 03_GEPD_processed \School\Confidential\Cleaned folder.
Note: These datasets are only meant to be used by the WB team and not meant to be shared publicly since they are not yet anonymized.
04_school_data_anonymizer anonymizes the data files produced from the previous step and stores the anonymized version of the four cleaned school-level data files in 03_GEPD_processed\School\Confidential\Cleaned\Anonymized. A user would need to tweak this do-file for each country before running it, this is an inevitable process, since part of the anonymization is country-specific. Information on what to tweak is listed inside the do-file.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
text:
8.5 - Cleaning public officials’ data
The process to clean public official data is nearly identical to cleaning the school-level data (Step 5). School data must be cleaned before the public officials’ files are cleaned. This is because the public officials are asked about teacher absence in the system and the answers are verified by checking against the GEPD teacher data.
The raw data files downloaded from Survey Solutions are located in 01_GEPD_raw_data/Public_Officials/public_officials.dta.
To clean the data, a user would need to execute two do files located in <<02_programs/Public_Officials/Stata>>:

The “01_public_officials_run.do” which will serve two functions:

verify if the profile.do is loaded to set up the macros and paths, and if not loaded then; the user will be asked to first run the profile.do on the same opened Stata console, then;
Will run and execute the second do-file to process the public officials’ raw data 02_public_officials_data_cleaner.do

Once the cleaning script is run successfully, the cleaned data can be found in <<03_GEPD_processed_data\Public_Officials\Confidential>>.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
text:
8.6 - Cleaning policy (experts) survey data
Meanwhile, expert data can only be processed using an R-script policy_survey.Rmd in /02_programs/Policy_Survey/R. At the top of the script, user would need to customize the information under “Country name and year of survey”. Detailed guidance on each step is given directly within the R-script. Note: to avoid problems with running any R script caused by directory set up, including the policy survey script, please open scripts using the Rstudio project titled GEPD_Production-countryname.Rproj, and found in the country’s folder.
Once the cleaning script is run successfully, the cleaned data can be found in <<03_GEPD_processed_data/Policy_Survey>>.

title: 8. Computing Indicators
text:
8.7 - Producing the GEPD key indicators
The GEPD’s indicators are contained in an Excel file along with a unique key for each indicator. This file’s purpose is to store the set of indicators published on the GEPD website and used for populating the standard GEPD PowerPoint slides.
Once the data (school – public officials – policy survey) has been processed from the previous steps, a user may proceed with running the indicators’ R-script which pulls all the cleaned datasets, aggregates them and produce a list of standard GEPD indicators. The R-script also organizes and stores this standard list of indicators into an (.xlsx) file and saves it under 04_GEPD_Indicators.
Prior to running the R-script, a user must make sure that three template files are already part of the cloned folder:

GEPD_indicator_template.csv; under sub-folder
<<04_GEPD_Indicators>>
Finance_scoring.xlsx; under
<<03_GEPD_processed_data/Other_Indicators>>
Learners_defacto_indicators.xlsx; under
<<03_GEPD_processed_data/Other_Indicators>>

The R-script is titled GEPD_indicators.R and can be found in 02_programs/GEPD_Indicators. Users need to edit the information the top of the script under “Country name and year of survey”. Detailed guidance on each step is given directly within the R-script.
Final indicators are available through the World Bank API. See https://databank.worldbank.org/source/education-policy.
